newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW- Mexico Q1 GDP suggests services firm.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW- Mexico Q1 GDP suggests services firm.

text.p: Mexico analysts on Monday welcomed first quarter growth in gross domestic product of 5.1 percent, adding this indicated the country's services sector was taking up the slack for a weaker industrial sector.
DAMIAN FRASER, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH, CASPIAN, MEXICO
"The number is higher than expected and is indicative of the services sector picking up. It is particularly good if you take into account the fact that there were fewer working days this quarter.
"It is thoroughly consistent with annual growth of 4.5 to 5.0 percent."
SERGIO MARTIN, CHIEF ECONOMIST FOR MEXICO, ING BARINGS
"It is a good number, and it reflects the previous consensus (Before Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz revised the first quarter forecast downwards last week).
"They moved expectations (downwards) and now it's above expectations, but if you take as a reference the 5.1 percent consensus earlier it is on target."

"The number reflects exactly what we saw with the industrial production figures: a slightly weaker growth in the economy than expected, basically due to a lack of credit and a weak recovery in consumer demand."
The Finance Ministry said the industrial sector led growth in the first quarter with a 6.2 percent gain.
Growth in the overall services sector was up 5.0 percent, it said.
A survey of Mexico City economists by Reuters found average expectations of a rise of a 5.12 percent for GDP.
